open.title: Name the science question v5.0 must answer
open.problem: Nobody has written down what EDX is for. The candidates pick different methods, different acquisitions and different truth data.
open.context: Candidates: (a) Mg/Si ratio per precipitate class (beta-double-prime vs beta-prime/U/B-prime); (b) Cu-bearing Q; (c) Si segregation at LPBF cell boundaries (chemistry without a diffraction boundary; the case where diffraction-guided smoothing fails); (d) solute depletion in matrix or PFZ. The owner's data hold 11-19 counts per pixel with sub-count Mg/Si, so every answer is a pooled one.

options.label: a — Mg/Si per precipitate class
options.consequence: Needs per-object or per-phase pooling on a registered pair, a separability matrix from the CIFs, the Al-Mg-Si CIF set; strategy S2. Effort +3-5 sessions over S1, medium risk (counts and registration).

options.label: b — Cu-bearing Q identification
options.consequence: Cu is the one clearly separable signal; S1 plus the B* table. Lower risk than a.

options.label: c — Si segregation at cell boundaries
options.consequence: Plain EDX on existing Velox files plus EELS thickness; no joint method needed on day one; G must not be used. Lowest effort.

options.label: d — matrix/PFZ depletion
options.consequence: Plain EDX, region pools, matrix blank; S1 only. Low effort.

open.recommendation: c first then a, because c is answerable on the 104 existing files the week the baseline lands, and a is the question the app's own precipitate pipeline is built around but needs an acquisition and a separability check first.
open.second_opinion: The completeness critic put this as P0-1: the choice picks S1 vs S2 and the acquisition route, so it goes first on the sheet. The second opinion warned that B* can relabel real beta-double-prime needles unless a separability matrix is computed before it is built.
open.question: Which one question should v5.0 answer first on your data?
open.default_if_silent: c then a; S1 is built, S2 pre-registered.

open.title: Acquisition route and the first joint field
open.problem: No usable 4D + EDX pair exists. The route that gets one decides the input path (same-file GMS vs cross-file registration) and the count regime.
open.context: R1 GMS STEMx + Super-X needs a second Esprit install, an ExternControl licence, IO firmware and a DDC swap (GMS EDS guide :724-869), unverified on a Velox-2.15 Talos G1. R2 Velox 4D-STEM needs Ceta-2 + the 4D option, never used. R3 Velox scan triggering an external camera (Duran 2023 on a Talos F200X + Merlin). R4 sequential: GMS 4D, then a Velox SI at the same field and tilt, possible today; registration works on the 190330 pair (peak 41.4, mirror + 90°). At the owner's 4D optics (0.26 nA) a simultaneous scan yields ~25-85 counts/px and 2-180x fewer X-rays per object area than his existing SIs.

options.label: a — R4 now: EDX SI at the 051 field and tilt, full stream, EELS t/λ map, two currents; ask service about R1/R2 in parallel
options.consequence: One microscope session, no new licence; gives the first registered pair, thickness and the Al-sum/Ar test; the same-file reader stays conditional.

options.label: b — wait for R1 (STEMx + Super-X) before any joint work
options.consequence: Blocks WP 4 and 9 for an unknown time and cost; fewer X-rays per object than R4; cleanest registration (identity + lag check).

options.label: c — both: R4 first, then a small STEMx test (.dm4 and .dm5) if service confirms
options.consequence: Two sessions; settles the file layout, identity/lag check and dm5 question; the science number still comes from R4 data.

open.recommendation: c, because R4 gives value immediately and the STEMx test is only for layout and the identity check, not for the science number.
open.second_opinion: The second opinion called the GMS same-file path speculative for this lab and the sequential route the likely real one; the critic added R3 and the per-area count deficit and asked the owner to get service answers before (i-a) is scheduled.
open.question: Do you book the R4 session at the 051 field now, and will you ask Thermo/Gatan/Bruker about R1/R2 and cost?
open.default_if_silent: c; (i-a) stays conditional in the plan.

open.title: Spectrum-only window and the Spectroscopy room mock
open.problem: Every EDX file the owner has is a plain spectrum image, but the app's window assumes a 4D cube (hasDataset == is4D, 29 uses in 13 files; the content branch is always two 4D panes). Without a spectrum-only window v5.0 runs on none of his data until he re-acquires.
open.context: The shell is frozen (ADR 035): WorkspaceView must change for a seventh room anyway (exhaustive switches), so the window structure must be in the mock the owner accepts. Width floor stays 915 pt if the spectrum pane accepts 180 pt; a wider floor moves the sidebar maximum and breaks NavigationSeamTests. Keyboard: Spectroscopy ⌘6 and Results ⌘7, or ⌘7 after Results.

options.label: a — spectrum-only window in v5.0, shown in the room mock now
options.consequence: +3-4 sessions incl. the primary-signal split; the mock shows both the attached and the spectrum-only layout; day-one value on 104 files.

options.label: b — attach-only in v5.0; plain SI later
options.consequence: Smaller frozen-shell change now, but opening a 1-29 GB cube just to look at a spectrum, and the shell is reopened again later at the same cost.

open.recommendation: a, because it is the only path to day-one value and ADR 035 makes a second reopening expensive.
open.second_opinion: Both the second opinion (§2.6) and the critic (P0-3) overruled the inputs analysis' 'owner's call, later slot' on this point.
open.question: Does the room mock include a spectrum-only window, and which digit shortcut does Results keep?

open.title: Data model: two signals plus a registration record, no dense cube
open.problem: Which representation holds an EDX spectrum image beside a 4D cube, where pooling happens, and whether a per-machine CSR cache is required.
open.context: M2 (two linked signals + Codable ScanRegistration against the 4D source grid, composed at use) is the only model that fits the owner's different-grid pairs. The Velox stream decodes once into a CSR store (0.24 GB vs 26.5 GB dense); Python decode of the 3.2 GB stream takes ~10 s. The record must allow a reflection (the 190330 pair registers at mirror + 90°). Velox already drift-corrects, so no frame re-alignment.

options.label: a — M2; pool by transporting masks onto the native spectrum grid; no dense cube; CSR cache optional until Swift decode is measured
options.consequence: Count-exact Poisson sums, no 1.8 GB cube, no new residency pressure on 8 GB Macs; a per-pixel joint method later needs the resampled cube added then.

options.label: b — M2 with M3 as a dense cache on the 4D grid (64 GB Macs), cache required from the first increment
options.consequence: Fast per-pixel fits later; +1.07-1.8 GB resident, combined-budget work now, cache purge policy against the lean-app directive.

open.recommendation: a, because it is simpler, exact, and defers the cube until a method needs it.
open.second_opinion: The second opinion proposed the mask-transport variant and dropping the frame alignment; the inputs analysis had M3 as a cache and a FrameAlignment record. The critic measured the decode time that makes the cache decision live.
open.question: Approve M2 with mask transport and reflections, with the cache decided after a Swift decode measurement?

open.title: k-factors: what quantification can honestly ship
open.problem: No k-factor source exists: Velox exports none, the owner's notebooks used placeholders, and theoretical k needs cross-sections and data rights. Without k there is no at% on any of his data.
open.context: Theoretical k from NIST EPQ data is public domain with a notice (third-party rights inside EPQ unverified). An internal standard would need a homogeneous solution-treated sample of the same alloy (existence unverified). Velox's own 20 % k rule. Count ratios (Mg/Si, enrichment over the matrix blank) need no k.

options.label: a — primary outputs k-free (net counts, Mg/Si count ratios, enrichment over the matrix blank, with intervals); typed k with source and date optional; theoretical k a later sheet
options.consequence: Honest numbers on day one, no data-rights blocker; no at% until a k source exists.

options.label: b — theoretical k from EPQ data in v5.0
options.consequence: at% on day one, +2-3 sessions, rights check on Bote-Salvat/Henke, 20 % systematic shown separately.

options.label: c — measure k on a lab standard first
options.consequence: Best accuracy; needs a standard the lab may not have and microscope time.

open.recommendation: a, because the decisive quantity for the owner's phases is a ratio and a ratio needs no k; b is pre-registered as v5.x.
open.second_opinion: The second opinion raised this as the missing decision M9 and the critic as P0-4; both agree the primary outputs must be k-free.
open.question: Do you accept ratios and enrichment as the v5.0 quantities, with at% deferred to a k source you approve?

open.title: Absorption correction on summed Super-X G1 data
open.problem: The owner's files hold one summed stream from four detectors. Refusing correction leaves Mg/Si biased by +3 % (30 nm) to +15-19 % (150 nm); correcting needs a geometry model the vendor does per segment.
open.context: Velox metadata carries azimuth 45/135/225/315°, elevation 22°, stage α/β and holder type; summing hides only per-quadrant shadowing. The bias is the same order as the gap between beta-double-prime composition models. Thickness comes typed ± σ or from an EELS t/λ map.

options.label: a — four-detector geometric average, badged, with per-quadrant take-off spread and thickness σ propagated; refuse only when geometry or tilt is unknown
options.consequence: Removes most of the bias; a residual shadowing systematic is shown as a term; ~1 session on top of the parity port.

options.label: b — refuse on summed data, show the uncorrected ratio and the estimated bias
options.consequence: No new physics, but every Mg/Si on his data carries a 3-19 % known bias.

open.recommendation: a, because the quantity of interest is the ratio and the bias is computable from the file.
open.second_opinion: The methods analysis said refuse; the second opinion (C9) and the critic (C7, C8) computed the bias and the available geometry and recommended the badged correction.
open.question: Ship the badged four-detector correction, or refuse and show the bias?

open.title: Parity and data-rights policy for the eXSpy port
open.problem: Which numbers are parity pins, which loss function the app uses, and where the line energies and mass-absorption data come from.
open.context: Integer window pins and closed-form CL/absorption pins are exact; LS model fits are a tolerance; HyperSpy's ML-poisson depends on optimiser and start (FePt Pt Lα 15229.7 vs 15351.6) so it cannot be pinned. exspy's line energies match Bearden to ≤0.022 % for Mg/Al/Si/Cu/O/Zr. Both exspy's FFAST MACs and its Chantler line energies are NIST SRD data with unclear terms; NIST EPQ ships both under a public-domain notice; xraylib is BSD-3. Repo rule: no user-visible parity toggle, inline DEVIATION notes.

options.label: a — exspy tables verbatim for parity; pins on windows, CL, absorption and LS fits only; science default Poisson-ML via IRLS; MACs and line energies sourced from EPQ with its notice; one science default, provenance names the estimator, no mode switch
options.consequence: Clean licence chain, no dead parity pins, one more table to maintain (EPQ copy) with per-line DEVIATIONs where it differs.

options.label: b — exspy tables and MACs copied as GPL data; LS everywhere; two user-visible modes
options.consequence: Fastest port; rights question on NIST data unresolved; a toggle the no-filler rule forbids; LS bias at low counts.

open.recommendation: a, because it resolves the rights question and the unpinnable-ML problem at once.
open.second_opinion: The second opinion rejected the two-mode switch and the second line table, and set parity on LS only; the critic widened the NIST question to the line table (C17).
open.question: Approve a: EPQ-sourced tables, LS-only parity, Poisson-ML default, provenance instead of a mode switch?

open.title: Joint-method scope for v5.0
open.problem: Which joint approaches ship in v5.0 versus later, given 25-85 counts/px at 4D conditions, an unvalidated phase map underneath, and per-phase scores not retained today.
open.context: E (pooling over objects/phases/groups/ROIs with the matrix blank) needs only a registered pair. B* needs an additive per-phase score output (PhaseVectorResult keeps winner + one runner-up; its score is a distance) and a separability matrix; a combined posterior needs a per-dataset calibration the threshold rule forbids shipping blind. D is cheap (PCA and k-means exist) and not pure noise at 2x2 binning. G and F have no precedent and synthetic-only truth.

options.label: a — E per phase/region (+H, I, K); per-object E only on simultaneous or sub-object-registered data; nothing else in v5.0
options.consequence: Smallest honest product; ~2-3 sessions after the baseline; the arbitration question waits.

options.label: b — a plus the B* table (no posterior) after per-phase score retention and a separability matrix, plus D behind an exploratory badge
options.consequence: +5-7 sessions; the open TESCAN-equivalent, inspectable; Gate B on the additive output; badges stack on the unvalidated phase map.

options.label: c — b plus G in v5.0
options.consequence: +6-10 sessions with no precedent; risk of smoothing away cell-boundary segregation; synthetic-only truth.

open.recommendation: b, because the table ships quantities and defers the calibration, and D costs little; G waits for a planted-segregation test.
open.second_opinion: The second opinion agreed on table-only B* and on deferring G/F, but narrowed B*'s reach (beta-double-prime variants probably inseparable; Mg/Si and Cu the robust signals) and asked for the separability matrix first.
open.question: a, b or c for v5.0?
open.default_if_silent: b, with B* contingent on the separability matrix showing a separable pair.

open.title: Thickness input and whether Spectroscopy includes EELS
open.problem: Absorption, the projection fraction f and the density goal all need a thickness per field or per object; the room name invites the question whether EELS (13 GB of owner SIs already exist) is in scope.
open.context: The GIF Continuum gives an EELS low-loss t/λ map at the same field cheaply; the DM SI reader built for EDS reads an EELS SI with signalType .eels at no extra cost; EELS analysis (zero-loss, t/λ, edges) is a separate port with its own GOS data that downloads from Zenodo.

options.label: a — thickness typed ± σ or imported from an EELS t/λ map as a scalar image; EELS analysis explicitly out of v5.0
options.consequence: No new science; one importer; the room name is honest if the docs say so.

options.label: b — EELS t/λ computed in-app from a low-loss SI
options.consequence: +3-5 sessions, GOS/data-rights work, a second parity target.

open.recommendation: a, because v5.0 needs the number, not the method.
open.second_opinion: The critic raised it as P1-11; no other report dissented.
open.question: Typed/imported thickness only, with EELS named out of scope for v5.0?

answered.title: v4.5 remainder that touches v5: the Velox .emd open, reopening the freeze, EDX = 5.0.0
answered.problem: The shipped v4.x app probably opens any Velox .emd as a one-row datacube (emulated from H5Reader's ordering, not driven); .emd is a registered Finder type and the owner has 2149 such files. ADR 049 freezes EDX; ADR 051 says v5 or v6; CI on main is red.
answered.context: A named refusal is a reader change + discovery-test cases under Gate B (1-2 sessions, can land in the v4.5 polish). CLAUDE.md asks for a reproducing observation before calling it a defect; the public velox_emd_version11 file is the reproduction fixture. The CI failure is a mechanical type-check split with no Gate D trigger.

options.label: a — reproduce on the public v11 file, land the refusal under Gate B in v4.5, fix CI, amend ADR 007 (EDX = 5.0.0) and reopen ADR 049 for v5 in the same sheet
options.consequence: One small lane before the cut; the owner's drive does not trip over it; v5 may start its ADRs and mocks.

options.label: b — release-note the .emd behaviour; fix CI; defer the ADR amendments to the v5 kickoff
options.consequence: No code before the cut; a known nonsense result ships; the freeze stays until a later sheet.

answered.recommendation: a, because the refusal is cheap, the reproduction is a one-file test, and the amendments cost three markdown lines.
answered.second_opinion: The second opinion (C11) insisted on reproduction before calling it a defect and judged the other two 'defects' to be hardening; the critic (C20, P0-6) emulated the open and listed the three v4.5 sequencing questions.
answered.question: Refusal in v4.5 or a release note; and may v5 ADRs and mocks start before v4.5 ships?
answered.default_if_silent: a; v5 ADRs and mocks start after the owner's drive, Core work after the cut.
answered.answer: Owner 2026-10-05: v4.5 ships as it stands, no drive first (ADR 052) — the Velox .emd behaviour is release-noted (reproduced at the reader), ADR 049's freeze lifts for EDX after v4.5, EDX = 5.0.0 (ADR 007 amendment), the CI split landed in the cut.
